feature: The shape settings say what they are
summary: Picking a shape now opens a section headed after that shape, with every color labelled by the part it paints, and the label stays put when the color comes from one you saved. The menu on a color offers only the saved colors meant for that part.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Flags are on by default (this rides next-styles). Nothing about how a shape paints changed, so an old document opens looking identical.

try.do: Press R and drag out a rectangle.
Read the section under Position & Size: it should be headed Rectangle, with rows Outline and Fill.
Press O and drag out an ellipse, then A and drag out an arrow, and watch the section rename itself and drop the Fill row.
Select the rectangle again and click the palette button on the Fill row, then choose Save as Style and name it Card.
Click the palette button on the Outline row: Card is not on the list, and the menu says your saved colors are for other parts.
Click the Card tile on the Library's Styles shelf and tick Outlines and text under Use it for.
Open the Outline row's palette button again: Card is now offered there too.

evaluate: Does the section header naming itself after the shape help, or does a header that changes as you click around feel unsteady?
With Card on the Fill row, can you tell at a glance which word is the part and which is the name of the saved color?
Is Color the right word for an arrow's one color, or should it say something else?
When a saved color is not offered on a row, is the menu's explanation enough, or did you go looking for the color you just made?
Do the two checkboxes under Use it for read as obvious, or is Outlines and text versus Fills and backgrounds too coarse a split?
rough: Where the mock was wrong: it hangs colors off a Fill section of its own. The app keeps them in the shape's own section, which is one place to look instead of two.

Scoping needed a notion of what a saved color is FOR, and there are two answers rather than three: ink (outlines, lines, text) and surface (fills, frame backgrounds). Saving records which, so nothing changes about saving one; the Use it for checkboxes are there because one blue really is both a button's fill and a link's color.

A color saved before this existed has no answer written down, so the app works one out: one of the app's own five keeps what the app made it for, anything else takes the parts it is already painting, and a color nothing uses stays offered everywhere. So an old document never has a color quietly disappear from every menu.

The color a row shows changes shape when it comes from a saved color: a wide rounded well you can click, versus a plain square you cannot. That is deliberate, because a styled color is edited in the Library, but the two do look like different controls in the same column.
Screen Recording was granted, so these are real captures. They are cropped to the section out of the full window shots the walk took; the whole windows are in /tmp/photonz-playtest/shape-settings.
The scoped menu itself is not photographed. A walk cannot click a control in the dock, so the filtering is proved by tests (ColorStyleRoleTests) rather than by a picture of the open menu.

The Measure section's own color row still uses its own narrower label column (44pt) rather than the shared one. Left alone: it is a different section with nothing to line up against, and touching it was outside this task.
